subject: Request: Launch Surge Overlay — structured short-run overage & rebate path
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finbatch.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch surge — temporary capacity + rebate ask

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well. We’ve got a product launch scheduled for Oct 12–14 and expect a short, high-concurrency spike during the three-day window (peak QPS projected ~3.5x our committed rate). Our internal ops lead asked whether Redwood can offer a structured short-run overlay: essentially a guaranteed burst slab for the window and a blended overage rate plus a small retroactive rebate if sustained usage drops back within committed thresholds in the following month.

Key asks:
- A confirmed burst slab (amount in tokens/qps) for Oct 12–14
- An overage rate for the burst that’s lower than pay-as-you-go (we’re asking for a blended/discounted surge rate)
- A mechanism for reconciling true-up and potential rebate (if our month-after usage normalizes)

We’re happy to sign a simple amendment or PO. I’ve attached the launch plan and estimated traffic profile. Can you let me know what’s feasible and an approximate price range today?

Thanks —
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Product Ops, FinBatch
Attachments: launch-plan.pdf (brief), traffic-estimates.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finbatch.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch surge — temporary capacity + rebate ask

Marta — thanks for the details and the plan. We can accommodate a short-run overlay for launch windows like this; I’ll outline a pragmatic path below and loop in legal/procurement for the amendment.

Proposal (high level):
- Burst slab: a fixed temporary allocation (example: +3x qps cap, 72-hour window) provisioned and reserved for the launch.
- Blended overage rate: instead of standard PAYG, offer a discounted surge rate for tokens generated during the window (proposed: 35% discount vs standard PAYG).
- Rebate true-up: if month-after average daily usage returns to within 110% of committed baseline, we’ll apply a one-time rebate equal to 50% of the excess overage charges during the window (applied to the next invoice or as a credit).

Operational notes:
- Measurement: metered by token-level logs and token-attribution to the request route indicated in the amendment.
- Billing cadence: upfront PO for the reserved slab + invoice for overage (offset by rebate if conditions met).
- Legal: we’ll run a short amendment (one page) that specifies the window, slab size, rates, and rebate trigger.

I’ve attached a quick pricing scenario (pricing-scenarios.xlsx) with numbers based on three slab sizes. Ben — can you confirm the numbers and draft the matrix we should present to FinBatch? Neha — can you confirm procurement/legal gating and what evidence/controls we should require for the rebate?

If that looks directionally right, Marta — can you confirm the exact launch UTC window and whether you want the slab size expressed in QPS or token budget? We can turn this into an amendment by EOD tomorrow if needed.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700

Rishi / team — quick numbers from the scenarios workbook:

Assumptions: baseline tokens/day = 120M; expected window spike tokens (72h) = +210M tokens
Options:
- Small slab (50% of spike): reserved +105M tokens, 30% overage discount -> estimated incremental cost = $14,800
- Medium slab (75% of spike): reserved +157M tokens, 35% overage discount -> estimated incremental cost = $21,600
- Full slab (100% of spike): reserved +210M tokens, 38% overage discount -> estimated incremental cost = $27,900

Rebate mechanics (operational):
- Lookback window: 30 days after the launch month. If average daily tokens in lookback <= 110% of baseline, rebate applies.
- Rebate = 50% of billed overage attributable to the launch window (applied as credit).

I’ve also added a quick sensitivity column for token-price variance and a HubSpot link for the opportunity: HS-10234. If FinBatch wants the simplest path, medium slab + blended overage keeps risk reasonable and is easiest to bill.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Pricing, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-scenarios.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700

Thanks — flagged a few procurement/compliance items we need to lock before we push the amendment:

1) Measurement & auditability: require token-level logs for the window with MD5 hashes preserved for a 90-day audit period. That’s the gating signal for a rebate.
2) PO path: FinBatch should issue an amendment PO that covers the reserved slab (we’ll invoice the overage separately).
3) Rebate timing: rebate will be issued as a credit within 45 days of the lookback period close, contingent on logs and a reconciled usage report.
4) Data residency: confirm that no customer PII will be routed through the special slab; if so, we need additional controls.

Attaching our compliance checklist for quick review. Marta — please confirm the PO owner and whether your legal wants a redline to the standard amendment template. If LegalPro will act as your counsel, we can also coordinate with them directly to shorten the timeline.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks, everyone — this is very helpful and directionally what we were hoping for. A few quick answers:
- Confirmed launch UTC window: Oct 12 00:00 UTC to Oct 14 23:59 UTC (72 hours).
- We prefer the medium slab option. Please prepare a short one-page amendment we can sign and I’ll have our procurement issue the PO once terms are final.
- LegalPro will be our counsel on this; I’ve cc’d them. They’ll review the amendment and confirm any redlines.

Can we schedule a 30-minute handoff tomorrow? I’m available 11:00–13:00 UTC. If you can send a one-pager and the pricing matrix beforehand that would speed the PO.

Appreciate the fast turn —
Marta
